statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-123611 (GHSA-w44r-93j7-qv28, RUSTSEC-2026-0349): rustls before 0.23.46 records the key-exchange group chosen in an unauthenticated ServerHello per server name, so a network attacker who answers one connection with a ServerHello selecting X25519 makes later ClientHellos send only classical key shares, losing post-quantum confidentiality. Fixed in rustls 0.23.46: https://github.com/rustls/rustls/security/advisories/GHSA-w44r-93j7-qv28, https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0349.html. Read the crate list that cargo-auditable embeds in /usr/bin/uv and /usr/bin/uvx of all 84 published uv packages in the DHI Debian repository, 0.11.22-0 to 0.13.9-2 for amd64 and arm64 (42 builds per architecture), each verified against the checksum in the package index; no debug-symbol packages are published for this source. The crate list of /usr/bin/uv names rustls 0.23.40 to 0.23.43 in builds 0.11.22-0 to 0.12.15-0, rustls 0.23.45 in 0.12.17-0 to 0.13.4-0, and rustls 0.23.46 in every build from 0.13.4-1 on; each list names a single rustls version, and both architectures agree for every build. Of the two programs in each package, /usr/bin/uv is the one that carries rustls code: /usr/bin/uvx is a small launcher that runs uv, and although its embedded list names the same crates, a strings search finds no rustls source paths in it in the 0.12.15-0 and 0.13.4-0 amd64 and the 0.12.17-0 and 0.13.4-1 arm64 packages, while the same search finds other crates' source paths (gimli, miniz_oxide) in /usr/bin/uvx and finds rustls 0.23.43, 0.23.45, 0.23.45 and 0.23.46 source paths in /usr/bin/uv of those packages. Every build before 0.13.4-1 is affected and every build from 0.13.4-1 on is fixed.
